entries.title: clawboo@0.9.1
entries.note: Patch Changes 919e2fe : When you take control of an agent's screen, a key you press right as control arrives is now let go if you switch to another window straight away. Before, that key could stay held down on the agent's display. 5563a96 : A dashboard opened around your sign-in proxy, on a server that counts only a person the proxy signed for, no longer says that moving cards is refused there. A card moved there does move; it just does not stop the run on it, which is what the notice now says.

entries.title: clawboo@0.9.0
entries.note: Minor Changes 27bf4fd : The dashboard's frame is reworked. An account bar runs along the bottom of the sidebar, under the team rail and the agent column: the person a sign-in proxy verified (or "You" on a local install, said as such), the theme switch and the Settings gear, which moved there from the agent column. The team rail is 72 px wide with larger icons, and its add-team button now sits at the end of the team icons and scrolls with them. An app that shows the dashboard in its own window can ask for a slim top bar by setting data-clawboo-embed-titlebar on the page, with --clawboo-titlebar-inset for its height and the new --clawboo-titlebar-left for the window buttons' width: the sidebar's hide button (moved there from the agent column), back and forward through the dashboard's own pages, the team or page name, Needs you and help. entries.title: clawboo@0.8.0
entries.note: Minor Changes 18e0659 : On Linux, each agent can now run as an operating system user of its own, so agents are walled off from each other as well as from Clawboo. Set CLAWBOO_AGENT_USERS to a pool of users you create once (names, or a uid range such as uid:20001-20008 ), CLAWBOO_AGENT_GROUPS to a pool of team groups, and CLAWBOO_WORK_DIR to a folder of your own. It is used instead of CLAWBOO_AGENT_USER , never with it, and is off unless you set it. An agent gets the next free user when it is created, oldest first, and keeps it for its life; each team gets a group the same way. Each agent user has an agent host of its own, started on the agent's first need, closed with the agent's processes after 10 minutes with nothing to do, and watched on its own: a host that stops answering costs only its own agent's processes. An agent's runtime homes, browser profile and display live in its own user

entries.title: clawboo@0.7.0
entries.note: Minor Changes 3cf2d73 : New connector: Cua Driver (category Desktop , Linux only) uses the apps on an agent's own screen through Clawboo's tool server: it lists windows, clicks, types and reads each app's accessibility tree. It runs only when agents run as their own OS user ( CLAWBOO_AGENT_USER ), like control links: it types into the agent's browser, which otherwise runs as you. Without it, agents still get their screen, the live view and their browser tools. Install it from an agent's Screen view, connect it, and give it to the agents that need it; it is not given to every agent. Each agent gets its own Cua Driver process on that agent's own screen, as the agent user when agents run as their own OS user, with a home folder of its own and the screen's own session bus, never your desktop session's. It runs only from Clawboo's own install, with its telemetry and update check turned off. A

entries.title: clawboo@0.6.0
entries.note: Minor Changes c9215fb : Restore archived teams and move agents between teams from the dashboard. Archived teams. The team rail ends with an Archived group listing archived teams, which were otherwise shown nowhere. Click one and choose Unarchive to bring it back. Move to team. Right-click an agent on the Org chart or a team graph and choose Move to team . The move happens in one step through the new POST /api/agents/:agentId/move : the agent's own routines go with it, tasks it has not started stay on the old team's board unassigned instead of firing at an agent that left, and its old rooms and session state are cleared. A routine bound to one of the old team's tasks is paused there instead of moving. A team's lead, Boo Zero and an agent with a task in progress or in review cannot be moved. 6ce571a : The Board is calmer and easier to read. It opens on Kanban, a dense status board with Nee

entries.title: clawboo@0.5.0
entries.note: Minor Changes fa4aa95 : The Board is now a calendar and a task board at once: the status columns run across the top and the days run down the side, so every card sits in its status column on its day. Days as rows. Week is the default view, starting on your locale's first weekday; Today shows today alone with every card in sight, and Month shows every day of a month. All is the same board with one row instead of days, every task newest first, with the same columns, lanes and cards. Open work sits on the day it was added and stays in its row as it moves across the columns; work that reaches Done or Cancelled moves to the day it finished. Open work from before the range is gathered in an Earlier row, so a later week never hides something still in play; it opens by itself when it holds work that is running or waiting, and otherwise stays folded with a note of what it holds. entries.title: clawboo@0.4.0
entries.note: Minor Changes a28711e : Gmail, Slack, Jira and thirty-eight more, through Composio. Apps clawboo cannot sign in to on its own now sit in their own band on the connectors page. Paste a Composio project key once, press Connect on an app, approve it at the provider, and it stays connected. Every connected app also appears as its own node on the graph, attached to the agents that can reach it. That last part is deliberate: a single node marked Composio would hide the fact that an agent can read your email, where a Gmail node says it plainly, and a thing you can see is a thing you can take away. This replaces a first attempt that did not work, and the reason it did not is worth writing down. entries.title: clawboo@0.3.1
entries.note: Patch Changes 8d96a6c : --- "clawboo": patch Team chat reliability, plus provider and model UX: Replies no longer vanish — every streamed team-chat reply now commits to the transcript (or is cleanly cleared), so a delegating agent's message can't disappear on the next update or on reload. A native 1:1 reply that fails mid-stream is preserved instead of silently dropped. Live Working/Idle badges — the sidebar agent and Group Chat status indicators update in real time for native / server-orchestrated team runs and native 1:1 chats, not just OpenClaw over a live Gateway. Runtime provider manager — the Runtimes panel's Manage view for Clawboo Native, OpenClaw, and Hermes lists the LLM providers you have actually connected (synced with Settings → Providers), each with per-provider connect/disconnect, one-click reconnect using an existing key, and a default-model picker for Native. entries.title: clawboo@0.3.0
entries.note: Minor Changes d543d11 : Native-first. Clawboo now runs Gateway-free on a single provider key: onboarding connects a key, optionally adds Claude Code / Codex / Hermes / OpenClaw, then deploys a real marketplace team. Adds a providers hub across ten providers with live model lists, per-agent runtime and model pickers, and a first-run capability tour. Native teams chat and delegate end to end, with orchestration running server-side so a cascade survives a tab close. The Ghost Graph gains runtime badges, model orbitals, and MCP connector nodes, so every agent surfaces its attached MCP and built-ins. A degraded Gateway no longer blocks the dashboard: a non-blocking banner offers the recovery that actually applies.

entries.title: clawboo@0.2.0
entries.note: Minor Changes The v0.2.0 liberated cut. Native agents are built in (paste a provider key, no external CLI), and OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes join as peer teammates in one chat, sharing one durable board, one tiered memory, and one capability dashboard, all governed and verified. Includes the team-task scheduler, per-runtime native homes, an encrypted credential vault under ~/.clawboo/ , and a release-cut security audit. See CHANGELOG.md for the full arc.
